answer: A timing-pattern cluster detector flags accounts whose transaction timing and fee choices form a tight, repeated spiral across separate wallets. After the fact, it joins identities through a shared withdrawal inlet and scores graph modularity; clusters above threshold are frozen pending review. An anchor cohort of known benign accounts calibrates that threshold, so attackers cannot shift the baseline cheaply. To evade detection, an attacker needs a separate funding source and randomized timing per identity, costing about two extra accounts and one delayed withdrawal per identity.
